issue_context.title: systemd-networkd Address=0.0.0.0/30 assigns too many addresses
issue_context.body:
### systemd version the issue has been seen with

252

### Used distribution

OpenSuse Tumbleweed

### Linux kernel version used

6.1.4-1-default

### CPU architectures issue was seen on

x86_64

### Component

networkctl

### Expected behaviour you didn't see

Once the `Address=0.0.0.0/30` has assigned an IP address, it does not assign another one.

### Unexpected behaviour you saw

At configure time `Address=0.0.0.0/30` configures two addresses. Over time more address ranges are added. Previous assignments are not recognized.

### Steps to reproduce the problem

1. `machinectl pull-tar --verify=no http://download.opensuse.org/tumbleweed/appliances/opensuse-tumbleweed-image.x86_64-networkd.tar.xz tumbleweed`
2. `machinectl clone tumbleweed test`
3. `machinectl start test`
4. Observe that the `ve-test` interface was created and has been configured by `systemd-networkd`.
5. Observe that it has _at least_ two configured IP addresses.

```
9: ve-test@if2: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1500 qdisc noqueue state UP group 666 qlen 1000
    link/ether d6:4b:72:ab:56:41 brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff link-netnsid 1
    inet 192.168.187.137/30 brd 192.168.187.139 scope global ve-test
       valid_lft forever preferred_lft forever
    inet 192.168.150.225/30 brd 192.168.150.227 scope global ve-test
       valid_lft forever preferred_lft forever
```

### Additional program output to the terminal or log subsystem illustrating the issue

This is the `/etc/systemd/network/79-container-ve.network` that is configuring my `ve-` devices. The builtin `80-container-ve.network` has the same problem.

```toml
[Match]
Name=ve-*
Driver=veth

[Network]
Address=0.0.0.0/30
LinkLocalAddressing=no
LLDP=no
LLMNR=no
IPForward=yes
DHCPServer=yes
IPv6AcceptRA=no
IPv6SendRA=no
```

the logs seemed to indicate that `address_pool_acquire_one` gets called twice, once when networkd initially configures the interface and once again when it gains carrier (when the other side of the veth is brought UP, I think?).
